title: Telemetry-gating oncall playbook: rapid throttle & key-guard
incident_summary: Working notes for an oncall-first approach to dealing with volumetric traffic floods and API key leakage-class abuse. Focus is on rapid telemetry gating (soft gates), automated minimal-impact throttles, and an operator checklist to escalate to WAF or account suspension only when necessary.
detection_rules:
1) Short-window spike: request rate per API key > 200 req/s for > 60s AND 95th latency < 1s -> suspect auto-burst test or abuse.
2) Key reuse across geos: single API key used from > 8 distinct countries in 10 minutes -> possible leakage.
3) Patterned traffic: identical prompt payloads or identical content-length + same user-agent across many IPs -> likely scripted abuse.
4) Error amplification: 5xx rate increasing by > 3x while success rate flat -> retry storm; backoff suggested.
5) Cache miss storm: token-level cache miss rate > 60% combined with throughput surge -> cold-cache traffic spike; consider prefix caching heuristics.
Notes: thresholds are intentionally conservative for initial soft-gates; tune with historical baseline per-customer and per-model. Use relative baseline (z-score) over 5m window when possible.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact oncall playbook for SRE to use during high-volume incidents that look like traffic floods or API key leakage. It's intentionally operational: short commands, quick queries, escalation gates, and post-incident follow-ups.

Quick mental model:
- Soft-gate = automated, reversible throttle applied at the ingress path (token bucket tweak, per-key rate cap) that aims to protect platform SLOs while minimizing customer impact.
- Hard-gate = account suspension, WAF block, or region-level blackhole. Use only when abuse clearly malicious or after consult with CS/legal.

Immediate triage (first 10 min):
1) Run the traffic fingerprint query (Datadog/BigQuery):
   - Datadog: timeseries(events.requests.count{env:prod}, "api_key", "5m") -> sort desc by rate
   - BigQuery quick: SELECT api_key, COUNT(*) AS reqs, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(client_ip) AS ips, ANY_VALUE(user_agent) ua FROM `prod_logs.requests` WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 10 MINUTE) GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY reqs DESC LIMIT 50;
2) Identify top 3 API keys and top 5 client IPs. Note geolocation spread.
3) Check model & route skew: are all requests hitting the same model/route? If yes, temporary route-level throttle can be less disruptive.
4) Check metrics: token-per-request, 95th latency, error rate, model queue depth. If token-per-request is very low (<20) and req rate is huge -> cheap spam; prioritize gating.

Soft-gate checklist (apply if suspect abuse or unknown large spike):
- If single key dominates (>40% of requests): apply per-key token-bucket of 10 req/s for 60s, monitor. Command: curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/keys/<key>/throttle -d '{"rate":10,"burst":20,"ttl":60s}' (ops only).
- If multiple keys but same requester IP subset: apply IP-based burst limit at edge (WAF or proxy) at 100 req/s per IP for 2m.
- If many countries and high churn: rotate API key (if customer agrees) or issue immediate customer notification template (see linked_artifacts).
- If error amplification (5xx): add server-side ingress adaptive backoff: scale down max inflight to protect model queues.

When to escalate to WAF or hard block:
- Confirmed credential theft: key seen across malware blacklisted ASNs or known botnets -> notify CS/legal and block ASN at WAF.
- Repeated soft-gate overrides: if the suspect source can bypass or continues after multiple soft-gates (3 tries in 20m) -> escalate to IP block or route-level denial.
- Financial exposure: if projected cost (estimated tokens * model unit cost) exceeds $5k in next 24h -> finance alert + immediate hard throttle.

Operator commands & quick queries (copy-paste):
- Top keys last 10m (BigQuery):
  SELECT api_key, COUNT(*) as reqs, SUM(tokens) tokens, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(client_ip) ips FROM `prod_logs.requests` WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 10 MINUTE) GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY reqs DESC LIMIT 20;
- Top identical payload hashes (possible spam):
  SELECT payload_hash, COUNT(*) c, ANY_VALUE(api_key) k FROM `prod_logs.requests` WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 MINUTE) GROUP BY payload_hash ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 50;
- Check model queue depth (Grafana): dashboard -> model-queues -> filter by model_name.
- Quick token cost estimate: tokens * cost-per-token(model) aggregated per key in query above.

Communication templates:
- Customer notify (short): "We detected unusual high-volume activity on your API key. We have applied a temporary protective throttle to prevent service disruption. Please rotate your key if you did not initiate this traffic. Contact support@redwood.com with the subject: Key Rotation Request."
- Internal alert (pager): include top 3 keys, top 3 IPs, approximate cost estimate, actions taken.

Post-incident follow-up (within 72h):
- Create a postmortem stub with timeline and attach key queries. Add a section: "Possible improvements" with: adaptive per-account baselines, automated key rotation API, better ASN blocklists.
- Engineering tasks: add a threshold-based automation to convert soft-gate -> hard-block after N overrides.
- Product tasks: review chargeback/overage playbook for customers affected by throttles.

Known gotchas and heuristics:
- PLG onboarding spikes: new customers running bench/scale tests can mimic abuse. Cross-check signup time and known trial accounts before hard blocking.
- Marketplace partners: some partners fan out requests through many keys — per-key throttles can be disruptive. Check partner whitelist.
- WAF false positives: aggressive regex rules on payload can break legitimate clients; prefer rate-based rules first.

Open questions / unresolved:
- What's the exact per-key default soft-gate value we want for multi-tenant models with low token cost? Current 10 req/s is a starting guess. Needs historical tuning per-model.
- How to safely automate key rotation for customers without human-in-loop consent if abuse looks severe? Legal sign-off required.

Appendix - short incident notes (example timeline):
- 2025-10-28 14:02: metrics alert: total req/s x5 baseline; 14:04 identified key K-2397 with 62% of traffic; 14:06 applied soft-gate 15 req/s; 14:08 95th latency stabilized; 14:25 key rotated by customer; 14:30 normal traffic resumed.
- Lessons: soft-gate prevented queue saturation and avoided WAF block. Need automated notify template.

If you are oncall and unsure, ping #sre with the subject line: [SRE|TRAFFIC] <top-key> <top-ip> so we have context in the thread.

Notes-to-self style: keep playbook lean. Expand detection rules into param-driven dashboards so we stop copy-pasting SQL.
